payload.recallText: I grew up in rhode island, the rhode island of the kennedies and the irish. We were catholic, and they were catholic. They were irish, and we were irish. I was in the backseat of my fathers car when it was announced on the radio that it was the anniversary of president kennedys death. I started to cry and my sister mckella told my father. My father pulled off onto the shoulder of the road and turned around to face me, tears visibly falling down his cheeks, and he stated "Don't ever be ashamed or feel bad for crying for that man!". I can still recall the time me and my family spent at my aunts back in the 70's. My aunt used to take me to her dream vacation spot just in front of the Kennedy center. We would sit on the beach, but not facing the ocean water. Instead, we would face the Kennedy center. My aunt would hold her binoculars as we sat on the sand and she would look at the people walking around, presumably the kennedys, and would use a pen and pad to jot down to try and figure out who it was that she spotted walking. She would figure out who it was and note any recent deaths utilizing trial and error to try and figure out who was walking. The water came and washed us away. A Kennedy picked us up in their boat, and I'd never have dreamed that three dots would come and rescue us before we transformed into our aunt.
